title: Partial folds of the split Cayley hexagon H(9) and large graphs of diameter five
description: Let Γ be the incidence graph of the split Cayley hexagon H(9) and τ a duality of order four. The quotient F = Γ/⟨τ ⟩ is a graph on 33397 vertices of maximum degree 10 and diameter 5; it identifies each point p of H(9) with the point τ 2p. We show how to undo this identification on any set of such pairs while keeping the diameter at most 5. For every bijection σ from the points to the lines of a generalized hexagon, the graph on the points in which x and y are adjacent whenever one of them lies on the image of the other has diameter at most 5. Choosing σ(p) between τp and τ−1p according to a colouring of the pairs, the partial fold that keeps a set S of pairs apart has 33397 + |S| vertices and diameter at most 5, and its degrees are determined by S and the colouring. Together with a blow-up of the points of the subhexagon H(3) and twin vertices, integer programming over these choices gives N(11, 5) ≥ 36563, N(12, 5) ≥ 41699 and N(13, 5) ≥ 50750 for the degree-diameter problem; the previously published lower bounds were 35203, 38167 and 44232.
